decisions.decision: The measured state, re-read by the coordinator at 76cfa91. There are exactly TWO places outside internal/api that put an application.Caller on a context (`grep -rn ContextWithCaller --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test.go`): internal/runner/orchestrator.go:39, which FABRICATES application.Caller{Role: application.RoleOwner, Subject: "runner-local-owner"}, and orchestrator.go:40, which builds a genuine runner caller from the Orchestrator's own RunnerID. Inside internal/api, the only Caller constructions are internal/api/auth.go:50 and :85 (RoleRunner, from a verified runner session header) and auth.go:59 and :99 (RoleOwner, from the IAP assertion or the preview-local owner bearer token). NO non-test code anywhere constructs a Caller with RoleScheduler. Every non-test appearance of RoleScheduler is on the ACCEPTING side, and there are thirteen of them, enumerated in d2.
decisions.rationale: Re-measured rather than taken from dp-v2-082 d3, whose own risk register said that if a transport producing a scheduler caller were found, its reasoning would weaken. None was found. Two further measurements change the shape of the problem and must be recorded: Orchestrator.RunFakeJourney -- the only code that drives a whole Capture-to-AcceptResult journey -- has exactly ONE caller in the whole repository and it is internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go:56, and cmd/runner/main.go wires no control plane at all (it prints 'no external control-plane wiring is enabled' and exits 2 without --fake, and with --fake it is a signal-waiting daemon). So the fabricated owner exists solely to let a test driver through the role gate.

decisions.decision: The full enumeration of operations that name the scheduler, measured, with the verdict for each. Application commands via callerActor: Capture (service.go:744) owner|scheduler; Plan (service.go:883) owner|scheduler; Prepare (service.go:987) owner|scheduler; Control (service.go:1303) owner|scheduler; Permit (service.go:1458) owner|runner|scheduler; RegisterRepository (repository.go:133) owner|scheduler; repository.go:223 owner|scheduler; repository.go:471 and :514 owner|scheduler; StartFraming (framing.go:123) owner|scheduler; RequestHumanInput (human_input.go:461) runner|scheduler, with the OWNER refused. Transport gates: internal/api/api.go:427 POST /v1/requirements/{id}:request-input runner|scheduler; api.go:463 POST /v1/requirements/{id}:start-framing owner|scheduler. Attribution: internal/application/caller.go:64-72 requestedBy maps RoleScheduler -- and ONLY RoleScheduler -- to domain.ActorTypeLoop. VERDICT: ZERO operations require the scheduler. Every command that names it also accepts a role a real transport already produces (owner, or runner in RequestHumanInput's case). ONE thing does require it, and it is not an operation: requestedBy is the sole producer of domain.ActorTypeLoop for a Requirement's RequestedBy (service.go:748, :841), a Repository's (repository.go:137, :204), a Requirement-to-Repository link's (service.go:852), a Control Intent's requester (service.go:1307, :1365) and a human-input answerer (human_input.go:577).
decisions.rationale: This enumeration is the judging criterion the brief asks for -- 'does an operation that names this role actually exist' -- applied exhaustively rather than by sampling. Its answer at the operation level is no, which is the argument for removing the role. Its answer at the attribution level is yes and decisive, which is the argument against: internal/domain/model.go:222-230 declares ActorType to 'distinguish an owner-originated request from a decision the loop made', and docs/product/definition.md:32 makes analysis, solution choice, prioritisation and decomposition the LOOP's responsibility. If the role were removed, ActorTypeLoop would become unreachable for all five of those stored fields and every Requirement the Loop itself captures would be recorded as owner-originated -- a worse attribution defect than the unreachability being repaired. Note what is NOT an argument: ActorTypeLoop is already reachable on a HumanInputRequest's AskedBy, because askedBy (human_input.go:406-420) maps RoleRunner to it as well. So the gap is precise: ActorTypeLoop is unreachable for Requirement.RequestedBy, Repository.RequestedBy, the link's RequestedBy, the Control Intent's requester and the answerer -- and for nothing else.

decisions.decision: The judgement is (a): the scheduler stays declared AND becomes a role a real caller can be. (b) -- removing the role from the declaration -- is REJECTED.
decisions.rationale: Three measurements decide it. (i) A declared responsibility names the role: contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml:6-8 says 'Increment decomposition/planning is intentionally not a public owner operation; it remains a loop scheduler responsibility'. That is a public contract assigning Plan and Prepare to the scheduler, and today's code contradicts it by accepting RoleOwner for both. (ii) A real identity already holds the role and already authenticates: cmd/control-plane/main.go:168-170 requires RECONCILE_IDENTITY, and internal/api/api.go:87-92 verifies POST /internal/reconcile against 'accounts.google.com:'+ReconcileIdentity, refuses any request carrying a runner-session header, and answers with the message 'reconcile scheduler identity required'. docs/operations/control-verification.md:49-55 names it 'a dedicated Cloud Scheduler OIDC service-account identity', docs/architecture/technology.md:162-174 fixes it at exactly one job, and contracts/deployment_preflight lists cloud-scheduler-jobs as required resource coverage. So the operational form the brief describes -- one owner, several machines, a management server that is owner-only but still requires authentication -- already contains one non-owner, non-runner machine identity, and it is the scheduler's. (iii) Deleting a declared enum member whose absence makes a DOMAIN distinction unreachable is a narrowing, not a measurement. The closed-set doctrine V2-065 wrote works in the widening direction: adding an entry with its reason is a measurement, removing one that carries meaning is a weakening.

decisions.decision: The producer is ONE new exported constructor in internal/application: LoopCaller(subject string) (Caller, error), which returns Caller{Role: RoleScheduler, Subject: subject} and refuses an empty subject with ErrUnauthenticated. It is the in-process analogue of internal/api/auth.go's transport constructors and is documented as the ONLY sanctioned way to obtain a scheduler caller. No other package constructs a Caller literal with RoleScheduler, and that count is asserted.
decisions.rationale: Measured reason a constructor rather than a bare literal: the two existing fabrication sites (orchestrator.go:39-40) are literals, and a literal is exactly how a component names itself. Funnelling the role through one named, refusing constructor makes the count of producers greppable and assertable -- which is how this task's own repair is measured, 0 producers before and 1 after -- and gives the refusal of an empty subject one home instead of none. It lives in internal/application/caller.go beside Role, Caller, ContextWithCaller and requestedBy, so it adds no import edge and no file.

decisions.decision: The transport that produces it is CombinedAuthenticator, the production IAP boundary. It gains one field, SchedulerIdentity string. Authenticate keeps its existing order -- runner-session header first, unchanged -- then, after parseIAPEmail succeeds, checks the scheduler identity BEFORE the owner-email map: when SchedulerIdentity is non-empty and equals the asserted email, it returns application.LoopCaller(email). An email that appears in BOTH OwnerEmails and SchedulerIdentity is a REFUSAL naming the misconfiguration, not a silent precedence. LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator is NOT changed.
decisions.rationale: Measured: CombinedAuthenticator is the only authenticator cmd/control-plane selects for a real deployment (main.go:179), and the reconcile identity is already an IAP-asserted email there, so the scheduler branch costs one comparison against a value the process already requires. Checking it before the owner map is required rather than stylistic: an identity that resolved as owner would silently gain every owner-only route, which is the same self-naming defect one level up. Refusing the overlap rather than ordering around it is what makes the boundary auditable -- a single asserted email must have exactly one role. LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator is excluded deliberately and the exclusion is recorded, not omitted: it establishes identity from bearer tokens, so a preview-local scheduler would need a new local-only environment variable and a new token map, and the outcome sentence asks for the role to be reachable, which the production boundary already satisfies. The preview-local composition can therefore produce an owner and a runner but not a scheduler, and that is stated in the evidence as a residual rather than papered over.

decisions.decision: POST /internal/reconcile keeps its existing inline identity check BYTE-FOR-BYTE and is NOT re-routed through h.config.Authenticator. What changes is that, having verified the identity it already verifies, it now carries application.LoopCaller(h.config.ReconcileIdentity) on the context it passes to h.config.InternalReconcile. api.Config gains no field and loses none; ReconcileIdentity keeps its exact fail-closed meaning (empty means 401).
decisions.rationale: Measured reason not to re-route it: the reconcile branch runs BEFORE the `h.config.Authenticator == nil` guard at api.go:113-116 and reads the IAP header directly, so it works under LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator too -- and that authenticator cannot resolve an IAP email at all. Routing the branch through the authenticator would break the preview-local composition and would change the behaviour the two existing negative tests at internal/api/api_test.go:85 and :93 pin. Carrying the caller instead is additive: every existing status code, body and refusal is unchanged, and the tick's identity becomes present and correct instead of absent. The honest limit, which the evidence must state: the reconcilers cmd/control-plane's closure drives (reconciler.Reconciler.Tick and reconciler.VerificationReconciler.Tick, main.go:184-189) take no Caller today, so the carried caller is verified as present and correctly attributed but is not yet consumed by any command inside the tick. The Requirement transitions that WILL consume it -- wait and recover, which docs/architecture/domain-model.md:267 and :270 define as automatic -- belong to the V2-084 follow-on, not here.

decisions.decision: internal/runner/orchestrator.go:39's fabrication is fixed, and it would have to be fixed under (a) and under (b) alike. Orchestrator gains a required field, Caller application.Caller; RunFakeJourney fails closed with the existing 'orchestrator dependencies are incomplete' style refusal when Caller.Role or Caller.Subject is empty, and builds the owner context from that field instead of from a literal. It is NOT relabelled RoleScheduler.
decisions.rationale: non_goals item 2 is 'do not let a component call itself owner in order to get through', and relabelling the literal RoleScheduler would satisfy the letter and violate the sentence -- it would be the same self-naming one word over. Injection is the repair: the identity comes from whoever constructs the Orchestrator, which is measured to be exactly one place and it is a test (orchestrator_test.go:56). The change is cheap and provably contained because cmd/runner/main.go constructs no Orchestrator at all, so no production wiring changes. Judged against the alternative of moving RunFakeJourney into a _test.go file: that is a larger, better change and it is NOT taken here, because it would delete a non-test exported method other tasks' evidence names, and because the outcome sentence asks for the fabrication to stop, not for the driver to move. Record the finding that the method is test-only so a later task can decide.

decisions.decision: The scheduler is granted NOTHING beyond what already names it. No callerActor pair is changed, no operation becomes scheduler-only, no new route is added, no PermitKind or role check is widened, and contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is byte-unchanged. The scheduler's reachable surface after this task is: POST /internal/reconcile (its own endpoint, whose reconcileScheduler security scheme is already declared at openapi-v1.yaml:10-13), plus every owner-or-scheduler and runner-or-scheduler pair that already names it.
decisions.rationale: non_goals item 1 is explicit. The temptation the measurement creates is to act on openapi-v1.yaml:6-8 by narrowing Plan and Prepare to scheduler-only, which would remove the owner from two commands and break every existing fixture that calls them as the owner -- 22 test files, measured. The declaration says planning is not a PUBLIC owner operation, which is a statement about the HTTP surface (where it has no route at all), not about the application-layer role pair. Reconciling those two is a separate design that must be argued on its own evidence; recording the tension is this task's job, resolving it is not.

decisions.decision: The proof is executed, over the composed HTTP handler with a real CombinedAuthenticator, and its centre is the attribution: a request asserting the scheduler identity captures a Requirement whose stored RequestedBy.ActorType reads 'loop', and GET /v1/requirements/{id} reports the same. The before/after measurement is stated as a count: non-test producers of a RoleScheduler Caller 0 -> 1, and reachability of domain.ActorTypeLoop for Requirement.RequestedBy false -> true.
decisions.rationale: This is the only assertion that makes the repair non-decorative today, and it is measurable in one run because requestedBy is the sole producer of that value for a Requirement (caller.go:64-72, service.go:748) and nothing produced the role. Everything else the task can prove is a negative: the same identity is refused on the owner-only routes (POST /v1/repositories, :answer-input), accepted on the pairs that name it (:start-framing, :request-input), an owner identity is still refused on /internal/reconcile, a runner-session-bearing request is still refused there, and an identity configured as both owner and scheduler is refused by the authenticator. Negatives are necessary but they cannot show the role does anything, so the attribution assertion carries the outcome.

decisions.decision: No read model change and no owner-console change. internal/application/readmodels.go, internal/web/** and docs/** are prohibited BY DESIGN. requestedByView (readmodels.go:136) already projects a RequestedBy with any valid ActorType, and domain.validActorType already admits ActorTypeLoop (internal/domain/model.go:235), so the new value flows through every existing response and export without a field, a branch or a document.
decisions.rationale: Measured: the actor_type value 'loop' is already declared in the RequestedBy schema and already validated by the domain, so the reason it never appeared was solely that no caller produced the role. That is what makes this repair small enough to be honest -- a repair that needs no read model, no schema and no document cannot have widened the surface. It is also why the change is observable through the field the existing dogfood and console already read rather than through a new one.

risks: The (a)/(b) judgement rests on d2's enumeration being exhaustive. If the implementer finds an operation that is scheduler-ONLY, or finds that domain.ActorTypeLoop is already reachable for Requirement.RequestedBy through some path the census missed, d3's reasoning changes and the finding must be escalated rather than absorbed. Do not resolve a disagreement by removing the role and do not resolve it by making an operation scheduler-only.

Checking the scheduler identity AFTER the owner map instead of before would let a misconfigured identity silently acquire every owner-only route. The order is load-bearing, and so is refusing the overlap rather than ordering around it: an identity in both OwnerEmails and SchedulerIdentity must produce an error, never a role.

Re-routing POST /internal/reconcile through h.config.Authenticator looks tidier and would break the preview-local composition, because LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator cannot resolve an IAP-asserted email and the reconcile branch deliberately runs before the authenticator-nil guard. The branch's own check stays byte-for-byte; only the context it passes on changes.

The carried loop caller is not yet consumed by anything inside the reconcile tick, because both reconcilers take no Caller. An implementer under pressure to make the change look load-bearing may be tempted to give the tick a command to call. That is the V2-084 follow-on's scope; here it must be recorded as a residual and the api record must say so plainly.

internal/api/api.go is held by V2-083 (queued) and internal/api/api_test.go by V2-087 (blocked on V2-083). Serialize V2-086 after both. internal/application/caller.go is prohibited to V2-082 and V2-085 but is this task's, so V2-085 must not be running concurrently either.

Adding a required field to Orchestrator changes a non-test exported struct. Its only constructor site outside tests does not exist, so the blast radius is the test files that build an Orchestrator literal; if any non-test construction is found, escalate rather than defaulting the field, because a defaulted identity is the fabrication again.
